raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation This PR speeds up Qwen3.8 (`Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`) decode on MI355X with ROCm. In a decode step of 8 rows or fewer, each of the 92 decoder layers runs as two persistent FlyDSL launches, ported from vllm-project/vllm#60833. Today each layer takes about a dozen kernel launches and two all-reduces, so small decode steps wait on launches and syncs. On one 8x MI355X node on `main`, TP8, no MTP, at 8k/1k, median TPOT drops **37% at concurrency 1**, with 56% more output tok/s. At concurrency 4 it drops 29%, with 40% more output tok/s. With NEXTN MTP, the second launch alone on the verify steps gives 31% more output tok/s at concurrency 1. The change is off by default, and `SGLANG_QWEN3_5_MONO_DECODE=1` turns it on. A step it does not cover keeps the existing path. These are prefill and mixed steps, steps of more than 8 rows, PP, and any setup other than TP8 on gfx950. With the flag unset, only `qwen3_5.py` changes on the default path. Its attention and GDN forwards now call `attention_core()` or `core()`, then `o_proj` or `out_proj`. These are the same ops in the same order. **Stacked on #43481.** That PR adds the Kimi-K3 mono framework, `k3_mono_flydsl/common` and `stages/gemv.py`. The Qwen kernels import it unchanged, so this PR does not carry a second copy. Only the commits after #43481 are new here. I will rebase once #43481 lands. ## Modifications - `kernels/ops/moe/qwen3_5_mono_flydsl/` has the K1 and K2 kernels of #60833 at `3346929b27` and their layout module, with the imports changed to `k3_mono_flydsl`. One change is new. K1 also takes a bf16 SSM state. It widens the state to fp32 for the recurrence and rounds it on store, as the stock GDN kernel does. The dtype is part of the K1 build key. - K1 (`gdn_pre`, 69 GDN layers) runs the residual add and input norm, `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba`, conv1d, the gated delta rule and the gated norm. It writes the input of `out_proj`. - K2 (`layer_post`, all 92 layers) runs `out_proj` or `o_proj` with an in-kernel TP all-reduce, the residual add and post norm, the top-10 router over 512 experts, the MXFP4 experts, the sigmoid-gated shared expert and the MoE all-reduce. - `srt/layers/moe/qwen3_5_mono_decode.py` binds the kernels to SGLang's state. It reads the GDN state from the mamba pool of the hybrid backend, with `mamba_cache_indices`, conv `(slots, dim, 3)` and SSM `(slots, HV, V, K)` in fp32 or bf16. The weight-layout options of #60833 stay off. These are the fused shared expert, MXFP4 `o_proj`, `out_proj` and `in_proj_qkvz`, and the output gate in K2. SGLang loads those weights as bf16 and applies the gate in `attention_core()`. The kernels skip pad rows, marked `-1`, and the reserved slot 0. The glue checks the weights once at the first decode step. When it turns itself off, it logs the reason. - `models/qwen3_5.py` splits `self_attention`, so `attention_core()` returns the input of `o_proj`. The 23 full-attention layers keep SGLang's fused HIP front and attention, then run K2. The GDN layer's `forward` splits the same way, and `core()` returns the input of `out_proj`. The text model's `forward` hands covered decode and target-verify steps to the mono path. The decode CUDA graph captures that path at widths 1, 2, 4 and 8. - `environ.py` adds `SGLANG_QWEN3_5_MONO_DECODE`. - The docs add the flag to `docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`. The glue checks these requirements at runtime: TP8, gfx950 and `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, because K2 runs the shared expert itself. Without speculative decoding, K1 also needs an fp32 or bf16 SSM state and no ReplaySSM ring. The glue also turns mono off on a GPU with fewer than 256 CUs, because a partitioned GPU cannot keep all 256 spinning CTAs resident. It does the same with HiCache or LMCache, because their copy kernels on another stream can hold CUs that those CTAs wait on. The launch argument checks raise `ValueError` instead of using `assert`, so `python -O` keeps them. Both changes follow the current #60833 head. This PR has a known problem on ROCm 10 images. The peer buffer uses aiter's `UncachedIpcHeap`, and its `load_hip_runtime()` opens `libamdhip64.so` by name. With `_rocm_sdk_devel/lib` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, that maps the devel HIP runtime next to the core copy that torch loads. This brings back the bug that #39513 fixed. `vattn_asm` binds to the first `libamdhip64` in `/proc/self/maps`, and #39513 assumed that this is always the copy of torch. Graph capture can then fail with this error. ``` RuntimeError: vattn_asm: hipModuleLaunchKernel failed: 709 (context is destroyed) ``` The failure needs all of these: - A ROCm 10 image with `_rocm_sdk_devel/lib` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. `rocm720` and `rocm724` images map one runtime, so they are not affected. - Mono decode on, so the peer buffer imports `UncachedIpcHeap`. - `vattn_asm` in use. That needs gfx950, the aiter backend, `--page-size 16`, head dim 256, and `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN` at its default of 1. Since #37465, `vattn_asm` runs plain q_len 1 decode (`forward_decode` calls `unified_attention_3d_mtp_decode_func`) as well as MTP target verify and draft extend. So non-MTP runs hit it too. Other page sizes do not use `vattn_asm`. The failure is intermittent. It broke two of three non-MTP server starts here, in the decode graph capture. [ROCm/aiter#6398](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6398) makes `load_hip_runtime()` bind to the copy that is already mapped. With that file mounted, no later start failed, with or without MTP. `smallm_moe_gfx950` looks up HIP the same way, so it is exposed too, but I have not seen it fail. #43481 imports the same `peer_memory.py`, so it also maps the second runtime on ROCm 10. ## Accuracy Tests The GSM8K, GPQA and NIAH results in this section used the earlier kernels, #60833 `f3c2ec988b`. GSM8K and NIAH for the head kernels are in the speed section. GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, `lm_eval` local-completions at concurrency 8. Flag on and flag off ran on the same image and node. | | flexible-extract | strict-match | | --- | --- | --- | | SGLang, mono on (this PR) | 0.8506 +- 0.0098 | 0.8287 +- 0.0104 | | SGLang, mono off (stock) | 0.8446 | 0.8302 | An exact per-question McNemar test, mono on against off, finds no difference. For flexible-extract, 87 questions are right only with mono and 79 only without, p = 0.59. For strict-match the counts are 81 and 83, p = 0.94. RULER `niah_single_2` at 128k scores 0.992 with mono on. With MTP, K2 runs only on the verify steps, as the MTP section below describes. GSM8K at concurrency 2 against the same MTP server with the flag off shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8582 against 0.8461, with 85 questions right only with mono and 69 only without, p = 0.23. Strict-match is 0.8446 against 0.8370, p = 0.47. GPQA Diamond and RULER `niah_single_2` ran at concurrency 8, so every decode step is in the mono range. Flag on and flag off use the same server config. | | flag off | flag on | | --- | --- | --- | | GPQA Diamond, thinking, temperature 1.0 (2 runs each) | 0.884, 0.924 (mean 0.904) | 0.894, 0.934 (mean 0.914) | | NIAH 64k (500 questions) | 0.994, 0.996 (2 runs) | 0.996 | | NIAH 128k (500 questions) | 0.996, 1.000 (2 runs) | 0.992 | GPQA samples at temperature 1.0, and the two runs of one arm differ by 4 points, so the 1-point gap is noise. NIAH is greedy. Paired per question, mono against each flag-off run gives p = 0.63 and 0.13 at 128k and p = 1.0 at 64k. The two flag-off runs also disagree with each other on 2 to 5 questions. No difference. The unit tests in `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_5_mono_decode.py` run on 1 GPU. They check that every fp4 byte and e8m0 scale of SGLang's gfx950 expert layout is where K2 reads it. K1 runs at widths 1, 4 and 8 against SGLang's pool layout. It writes the live rows and leaves pad rows and other slots unchanged. With a bf16 state, K1 gives the same core output and conv state as with the widened fp32 state. Its new state equals the new fp32 state rounded to bf16. The tests pass on MI355X in the v0.5.21-based image and on `main`, here the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09 with this branch's files. The file has not run in CI yet. The batch-invariance test in `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_5_mono_batch_invariance.py` runs K1 on 1 GPU and K2 on 8 GPUs. It keeps one probe row fixed and changes the other rows of the step. The probe outputs must be bitwise the same at widths 1 to 8, and equal to the probe run alone. It passes on MI355X on the ROCm 10 `main` nightly. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The numbers in this section are for the head kernels, #60833 `3346929b27`. `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` ran on one 8x MI355X node, TP8, on `main`, here the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09 with this branch's files mounted in both arms. The load is `bench_serving` random, range ratio 0.8, with the same seeds in both arms and one short warm-up cell first. Both servers use the aiter attention backend at page size 16, FSE off and a bf16 SSM state, and only the flag differs. They ran on the same node, back to back. | Cell (prompts) | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Change | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 (8) | 10.88 / 6.86 | -37.0% | 89.3 / 139.2 | +56.0% | | 8k/1k c2 (16) | 12.10 / 8.21 | -32.1% | 158.2 / 230.4 | +45.6% | | 8k/1k c4 (32) | 14.42 / 10.20 | -29.3% | 265.9 / 372.7 | +40.2% | | 8k/1k c8 (64) | 17.08 / 14.37 | -15.9% | 446.8 / 530.4 | +18.7% | | 8k/1k c16 (96), 16 rows: stock path | 23.59 / 23.55 | -0.1% | 650.7 / 655.4 | +0.7% | | 60k/600 c4 (32) | 25.77 / 21.52 | -16.5% | 132.1 / 154.0 | +16.6% | c16 decode steps have more than 8 rows, so they take the stock layers, and that row is the noise floor. TTFT does not change, because prefill is stock. GSM8K on the same servers, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, `lm_eval` local-completions at concurrency 8, shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8491 off against 0.8582 on, paired McNemar p = 0.36. Strict-match is 0.8370 against 0.8476. RULER `niah_single_2` at concurrency 8 scores 0.994 / 0.996 off and 0.992 / 0.998 on, at 64k / 128k. By default on `main`, this checkpoint runs without shared-expert fusion and with an fp32 SSM state, so a default server meets the K2 requirements as it is. These runs set `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` in both arms. ### MTP With speculative decoding on, K1 is off and K2 runs alone on the target-verify steps. GDN layers run SGLang's own input projection and core, then K2 runs `out_proj` and the MoE. K1 cannot run there, because it has no per-draft-token state for the SSM rollback. NEXTN runs 3 draft steps with top-k 1, so a verify step has 4 rows per request, one for each of the 4 draft tokens. Mono covers only c1 with 4 rows and c2 with 8 rows. The K1 requirements on the SSM state dtype and the ReplaySSM ring do not apply then. The MTP A/B uses the same setup plus `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`, so the reference is the same server without the flag. | Cell (prompts) | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Change | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 (8) | 3.87 / 2.88 | -25.7% | 237.8 / 312.1 | +31.2% | | 8k/1k c2 (16) | 4.64 / 3.82 | -17.7% | 391.2 / 463.9 | +18.6% | | 8k/1k c4 (32), 16 rows: stock path | 6.27 / 6.27 | flat | 590.3 / 591.9 | +0.3% | | 60k/600 c1 (8) | 3.95 / 2.97 | -24.9% | 114.4 / 129.3 | +13.0% | The accept length is the same in both arms, 3.62-3.68. GSM8K at concurrency 2 on the same servers shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8597 off against 0.8567 on, paired McNemar p = 0.82. Strict-match is 0.8438 against 0.8446. ### Earlier kernels
The first A/Bs used the #60833 f3c2ec988b kernels. Their tables stay here for reference. The table below compares the first kernels, `f3c2ec988b`, with the next #60833 kernels, `6a1c13b2fc`. Both arms ran on one MI355X node on `main`, the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09 with this branch's files, with a bf16 SSM state and the flag on. | Cell | Median TPOT earlier / new kernels (ms) | Change | Output tok/s earlier / new | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 | 7.77 / 6.88 | -11.5% | 123.4 / 138.0 | +11.8% | | 8k/1k c2 | 9.29 / 8.26 | -11.1% | 203.6 / 227.6 | +11.8% | | 8k/1k c4 | 12.04 / 10.33 | -14.2% | 317.0 / 368.5 | +16.3% | | 8k/1k c8 | 16.56 / 14.50 | -12.4% | 443.0 / 516.9 | +16.7% | | 8k/1k c16, stock path | 23.90 / 23.88 | flat | 643.3 / 645.7 | flat | | 60k/600 c4 | 23.93 / 22.16 | -7.4% | 139.9 / 148.8 | +6.4% | | MTP 8k/1k c1 | 3.26 / 2.90 | -11.0% | 277.8 / 308.3 | +10.9% | | MTP 8k/1k c2 | 4.30 / 3.78 | -12.1% | 418.9 / 469.5 | +12.1% | The whole gain is in K2. In a profile at one row, a K2 launch takes 39.2 us against 50.0 us before. K1 alone measures the same as before. GSM8K paired per question, earlier against new kernels, shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8423 / 0.8537 (p = 0.26) without MTP and 0.8393 / 0.8506 (p = 0.27) with MTP. Strict-match gives p = 0.88 and 0.94. The first A/Bs ran on a v0.5.21-based ROCm image with the same change and the `f3c2ec988b` kernels. That image has identical glue, and the `qwen3_5.py` hunks on its v0.5.21 file. I repeated both A/Bs on `main`, and the results agree. `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, 8x MI355X, TP8, no MTP, `bench_serving` random, range ratio 0.8, the same seeds in both arms. Both servers have FSE off and an fp32 SSM state, and only the flag differs. They ran on the same node, back to back. | Cell (prompts) | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Change | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 (8) | 10.66 / 7.65 | -28.2% | 91.2 / 125.9 | +38.0% | | 8k/1k c2 (16) | 11.68 / 9.12 | -21.9% | 163.8 / 208.3 | +27.2% | | 8k/1k c4 (32), first cell | 14.20 / 11.97 | -15.7% | 265.8 / 265.7 | flat, see below | | 8k/1k c4 (32), warm server | 14.18 / 11.91 | -16.0% | 270.6 / 321.4 | +18.8% | | 8k/1k c8 (64) | 17.51 / 16.39 | -6.4% | 437.6 / 469.1 | +7.2% | | 8k/1k c16 (96), 16 rows: stock path | 23.34 / 23.13 | -0.9% | 656.9 / 664.3 | +1.1% | | 60k/600 c4 (32) | 25.34 / 23.07 | -9.0% | 134.1 / 145.5 | +8.5% | c16 decode steps have more than 8 rows, so they take the stock layers, and that row is the noise floor. TTFT does not change, because prefill is stock. The first c4 cell is flat because of a one-time stall that this PR does not cause. Every server pays 15-40 s on its first prefills, flag on or off. The flag-off server happened to pay it during its startup warm-up request. The stall lines up with first-use JIT compiles on the GDN prefill path. The warm-server row runs one short c4 warm-up cell first. There, Max ITL is 726 ms off and 721 ms on, and the throughput gain matches the TPOT gain. The same A/B on `main` ran on the same node as above, with the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09, this branch's files mounted in both arms and one warm-up cell first. | Cell (prompts) | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Change | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 (8) | 10.99 / 7.76 | -29.4% | 88.5 / 123.6 | +39.7% | | 8k/1k c2 (16) | 12.25 / 9.25 | -24.5% | 156.4 / 205.7 | +31.5% | | 8k/1k c4 (32) | 14.63 / 12.05 | -17.6% | 262.3 / 317.6 | +21.1% | | 8k/1k c8 (64) | 17.30 / 16.48 | -4.7% | 441.2 / 466.6 | +5.7% | | 8k/1k c16 (96), 16 rows: stock path | 23.84 / 23.92 | +0.3% | 643.9 / 644.1 | flat | | 60k/600 c4 (32) | 25.95 / 23.38 | -9.9% | 131.2 / 143.8 | +9.5% | GSM8K on `main` with the same servers shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8582 off against 0.8605 on, with 88 questions right only with mono and 85 only without, p = 0.88. Strict-match is 0.8408 against 0.8415, p = 1.0. #### MTP with the earlier kernels Both arms ran on the same node with FSE off and `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`, so the reference is the same server without the flag. | Cell | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 | 3.77 / 3.21 | 244.5 / 283.3 | +15.9% | | 8k/1k c2 | 4.56 / 4.39 | 400.2 / 413.0 | +3.2% | | 8k/1k c4 (16 rows: stock path) | 6.05 / 6.01 | 608.5 / 606.7 | flat | | 60k/600 c1 | 3.85 / 3.29 | 117.3 / 125.2 | +6.7% | The accept length is the same in both arms, 3.62-3.69. Stock MTP with FSE on gets 3.37 / 4.21 / 5.70 / 3.45 ms TPOT. Its accept length on this random dataset is 3.96-4.00, so its TPOT is not comparable per token. Per verify step, which is TPOT times accept length, K2 saves 14-15% at c1 and 4% at c2 against both. The same A/B on `main` ran on the same node, with the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09 and this branch's files mounted in both arms. The accept length is 3.62-3.69 in both. | Cell | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 | 3.88 / 3.25 | 236.9 / 279.7 | +18.0% | | 8k/1k c2 | 4.62 / 4.29 | 391.0 / 419.0 | +7.1% | | 8k/1k c4 (16 rows: stock path) | 6.31 / 6.28 | 588.0 / 589.3 | flat | | 60k/600 c1 | 3.97 / 3.33 | 114.0 / 123.3 | +8.1% | GSM8K at concurrency 2 on `main` shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8506 off against 0.8499 on, p = 1.0. Strict-match is 0.8385 against 0.8324, p = 0.57.
## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The flag is in the AMD & ROCm table of `environment_variables.mdx`. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Done for MI355X with paired GSM8K, GPQA Diamond and NIAH accuracy, and speed with and without MTP, on the v0.5.21-based image and on `main`. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: **Missing `run-ci` label** -- add it to run CI tests. Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: **Blocked** -- `run-ci` is required first. Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.

nodes.body:
### MI355X verification of `d9945f4a4c` (TP8, no MTP)

Mono decode engages on all 8 ranks. Median TPOT drops 36% at 8k/1k c1, and GSM8K does not change (exact McNemar p = 0.71). Up to c8, flag-off TPOT is within 2% of the description's `main` table, and flag-on TPOT is within 4% of its new-kernel numbers (those used a bf16 state).

**Setup**
- Image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm720-mi35x-20261009` (`sha256:3d9129547126…`), with `/sgl-workspace/sglang` (editable install) checked out at `d9945f4a4c`. ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, Triton 3.7.0 (`git89002410`), aiter `e7d2453f25`, flydsl 0.3.4.1.
- One 8x MI355X node (gfx950, 256 CUs per GPU), host amdgpu 6.16.13. One server on the node at a time, with 8/8 GPUs idle over 30 one-second `amd-smi` samples before each server.
- `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, `--tp-size 8 --trust-remote-code --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-shared-experts-fusion` in both arms. The SSM state is fp32 (the checkpoint's `mamba_ssm_dtype`), attention is aiter with page size 1, and there is no MTP. Only `SGLANG_QWEN3_5_MONO_DECODE=1` differs between arms.

**Unit tests:** `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_5_mono_decode.py` passes 5/5 on one MI355X.

**Engagement:** all 8 ranks log `Qwen3.8 mono decode on for decode steps of <= 8 rows`, then `step at width 1`, `2`, `4` and `8` during decode graph capture. No `off` or `skips a decode step` message and no error appeared.

**Speed:** `sglang.benchmark.serving`, random 8k/1k, range ratio 0.8, seed 1, one warm-up row first. One round: flag off, then flag on, then the default server, back to back on the same node.

| Cell (prompts) | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Change | Output tok/s off / on | Change | Median TTFT off / on (ms) | Median TPOT stock default (ms) | Mono vs default |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8k/1k c1 (8) | 11.21 / 7.13 | −36.4% | 87.4 / 136.0 | +55.5% | 170 / 162 | 11.22 | −36.5% |
| 8k/1k c2 (16) | 12.30 / 8.29 | −32.6% | 157.9 / 232.1 | +47.0% | 328 / 319 | 12.33 | −32.8% |
| 8k/1k c4 (32) | 14.35 / 10.05 | −30.0% | 265.8 / 378.0 | +42.2% | 332 / 336 | 14.34 | −29.9% |
| 8k/1k c8 (64) | 17.47 / 14.27 | −18.3% | 439.9 / 540.9 | +23.0% | 388 / 382 | 17.44 | −18.2% |
| 8k/1k c16 (96), wider than 8 rows | 22.13 / 22.14 | +0.1% | 670.7 / 675.5 | +0.7% | 349 / 357 | 22.13 | +0.0% |

The default server (no `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, no flag) logs `Qwen3.5: shared-expert fusion not supported for this checkpoint (multi-streaming #25885 still applies). Shared experts fusion optimization is disabled.` and keeps the fp32 SSM state. It therefore matches the flag-off server within 0.3% on every row, and the flag-on server is faster than the default up to c8. The c8 and c16 cost in the description's "stock default" table (FSE on, bf16 SSM state) does not appear at this branch's base, where the default server already meets both preconditions.

**Accuracy:** GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, greedy, parallel 8, with `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` rather than `lm_eval`, so absolute scores differ from the description's: 0.936 with the flag off and 0.939 with it on. Per question, 35 are right only with mono and 31 only without; the exact McNemar p is 0.71. 151/1319 generations are byte-identical. This PR does not claim bit-exactness with the stock path, so I compared per-question correctness instead.

**Not covered:** MTP (K2 on target-verify steps), the bf16 SSM state end to end (only the unit test covers it), and the ROCm 10 `vattn_asm` issue: this image is ROCm 7.2 and page size 1 keeps `vattn_asm` out of the path, so ROCm/aiter#6398 was not exercised.

Thanks! Since #44353 landed, model monokernels live in sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono and are selected with `--monokernel-backend amd`, so this should become a Qwen3.8 spec there instead of the `SGLANG_QWEN3_5_MONO_DECODE` switch and the glue in `qwen3_5.py`. sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#6 (GLM-5.3-Flash) is the template.

- The runtime checks (TP8, gfx950, `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`) become spec data (`DeviceLimits.tp_sizes`, `Requirements.server_args`), so an unsupported setup is refused at startup with its reasons.
- Steps over 8 rows and other uncovered steps already take the normal path through the framework's routing.
- This stacks on #43481 (Kimi K3); the shared FlyDSL kernels should land in the plugin once, for both.
- The intermittent `vattn_asm` launch failure (ROCm/aiter#6398) is separate from the port.

Thanks @kevin-mii, agreed. We will port this to sgl-amd-mono as a Qwen3.8 spec, and drop `SGLANG_QWEN3_5_MONO_DECODE` and the hooks in `qwen3_5.py`. Thanks also @jhinpan for the independent MI355X run.

The plan for the spec:
- `gfx950`: widths 1-8 rows, TP 8, 256 resident blocks.
- `SPECULATIVE_DECODING`: target-verify steps run K2 only. GDN layers run SGLang's own GDN core there, so the rollback state is the stock one.
- An unfused shared expert for now, we can turn it on when https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41899 lands.
- Every K1 / K2 wait goes through `Mailbox.poll`, so the guard is a small change. We will show the guarded kernels bitwise against the current ones and re-run the A/B.

Questions:
1. The forward needs the `out_proj` / `o_proj` input. This PR splits `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet.forward` into `core()` + `out_proj`, and `Qwen3_5AttentionDecoderLayer.self_attention` into `attention_core()` + `o_proj`, with no behavior change. Is a small SGLang refactor PR with only that split OK? The other way is for the spec to rebuild both cores from `_prepare_qkv_gate`, `attn` and the GDN internals, which means more names in `SGLANG_READS`.
2. Shared FlyDSL code: our kernels also need `stages/gemv.py`, `sync.shift`, `plan.KernelAbi`, `ops.wave_sum`, `ops.wave_max` and `ops.block_excl_scan` from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43481, which `sgl_amd_mono/common` does not have yet. Should these go into `common/` in one PR before the three specs? We can send it, after we agree with @billishyahao and @vorapolsiloai, and check it against the DeepSeek-V4.1 plugin PRs that @amd-pedghazi plans.
3. Layout: one `qwen38/` package with the MoE and dense specs on shared `gfx950/` stages (as vllm#60833 now does with `MoeDims` / `GdnDims`), or one package per spec?

detail.body:
## Motivation This PR speeds up Qwen3.8 (`Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`) decode on MI355X with ROCm. In a decode step of 8 rows or fewer, each of the 92 decoder layers runs as two persistent FlyDSL launches, ported from vllm-project/vllm#60833. Today each layer takes about a dozen kernel launches and two all-reduces, so small decode steps wait on launches and syncs. On one 8x MI355X node on `main`, TP8, no MTP, at 8k/1k, median TPOT drops **37% at concurrency 1**, with 56% more output tok/s. At concurrency 4 it drops 29%, with 40% more output tok/s. With NEXTN MTP, the second launch alone on the verify steps gives 31% more output tok/s at concurrency 1. The change is off by default, and `SGLANG_QWEN3_5_MONO_DECODE=1` turns it on. A step it does not cover keeps the existing path. These are prefill and mixed steps, steps of more than 8 rows, PP, and any setup other than TP8 on gfx950. With the flag unset, only `qwen3_5.py` changes on the default path. Its attention and GDN forwards now call `attention_core()` or `core()`, then `o_proj` or `out_proj`. These are the same ops in the same order. **Stacked on #43481.** That PR adds the Kimi-K3 mono framework, `k3_mono_flydsl/common` and `stages/gemv.py`. The Qwen kernels import it unchanged, so this PR does not carry a second copy. Only the commits after #43481 are new here. I will rebase once #43481 lands. ## Modifications - `kernels/ops/moe/qwen3_5_mono_flydsl/` has the K1 and K2 kernels of #60833 at `3346929b27` and their layout module, with the imports changed to `k3_mono_flydsl`. One change is new. K1 also takes a bf16 SSM state. It widens the state to fp32 for the recurrence and rounds it on store, as the stock GDN kernel does. The dtype is part of the K1 build key. - K1 (`gdn_pre`, 69 GDN layers) runs the residual add and input norm, `in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba`, conv1d, the gated delta rule and the gated norm. It writes the input of `out_proj`. - K2 (`layer_post`, all 92 layers) runs `out_proj` or `o_proj` with an in-kernel TP all-reduce, the residual add and post norm, the top-10 router over 512 experts, the MXFP4 experts, the sigmoid-gated shared expert and the MoE all-reduce. - `srt/layers/moe/qwen3_5_mono_decode.py` binds the kernels to SGLang's state. It reads the GDN state from the mamba pool of the hybrid backend, with `mamba_cache_indices`, conv `(slots, dim, 3)` and SSM `(slots, HV, V, K)` in fp32 or bf16. The weight-layout options of #60833 stay off. These are the fused shared expert, MXFP4 `o_proj`, `out_proj` and `in_proj_qkvz`, and the output gate in K2. SGLang loads those weights as bf16 and applies the gate in `attention_core()`. The kernels skip pad rows, marked `-1`, and the reserved slot 0. The glue checks the weights once at the first decode step. When it turns itself off, it logs the reason. - `models/qwen3_5.py` splits `self_attention`, so `attention_core()` returns the input of `o_proj`. The 23 full-attention layers keep SGLang's fused HIP front and attention, then run K2. The GDN layer's `forward` splits the same way, and `core()` returns the input of `out_proj`. The text model's `forward` hands covered decode and target-verify steps to the mono path. The decode CUDA graph captures that path at widths 1, 2, 4 and 8. - `environ.py` adds `SGLANG_QWEN3_5_MONO_DECODE`. - The docs add the flag to `docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`. The glue checks these requirements at runtime: TP8, gfx950 and `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, because K2 runs the shared expert itself. Without speculative decoding, K1 also needs an fp32 or bf16 SSM state and no ReplaySSM ring. The glue also turns mono off on a GPU with fewer than 256 CUs, because a partitioned GPU cannot keep all 256 spinning CTAs resident. It does the same with HiCache or LMCache, because their copy kernels on another stream can hold CUs that those CTAs wait on. The launch argument checks raise `ValueError` instead of using `assert`, so `python -O` keeps them. Both changes follow the current #60833 head. This PR has a known problem on ROCm 10 images. The peer buffer uses aiter's `UncachedIpcHeap`, and its `load_hip_runtime()` opens `libamdhip64.so` by name. With `_rocm_sdk_devel/lib` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, that maps the devel HIP runtime next to the core copy that torch loads. This brings back the bug that #39513 fixed. `vattn_asm` binds to the first `libamdhip64` in `/proc/self/maps`, and #39513 assumed that this is always the copy of torch. Graph capture can then fail with this error. ``` RuntimeError: vattn_asm: hipModuleLaunchKernel failed: 709 (context is destroyed) ``` The failure needs all of these: - A ROCm 10 image with `_rocm_sdk_devel/lib` on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. `rocm720` and `rocm724` images map one runtime, so they are not affected. - Mono decode on, so the peer buffer imports `UncachedIpcHeap`. - `vattn_asm` in use. That needs gfx950, the aiter backend, `--page-size 16`, head dim 256, and `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN` at its default of 1. Since #37465, `vattn_asm` runs plain q_len 1 decode (`forward_decode` calls `unified_attention_3d_mtp_decode_func`) as well as MTP target verify and draft extend. So non-MTP runs hit it too. Other page sizes do not use `vattn_asm`. The failure is intermittent. It broke two of three non-MTP server starts here, in the decode graph capture. [ROCm/aiter#6398](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6398) makes `load_hip_runtime()` bind to the copy that is already mapped. With that file mounted, no later start failed, with or without MTP. `smallm_moe_gfx950` looks up HIP the same way, so it is exposed too, but I have not seen it fail. #43481 imports the same `peer_memory.py`, so it also maps the second runtime on ROCm 10. ## Accuracy Tests The GSM8K, GPQA and NIAH results in this section used the earlier kernels, #60833 `f3c2ec988b`. GSM8K and NIAH for the head kernels are in the speed section. GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, `lm_eval` local-completions at concurrency 8. Flag on and flag off ran on the same image and node. | | flexible-extract | strict-match | | --- | --- | --- | | SGLang, mono on (this PR) | 0.8506 +- 0.0098 | 0.8287 +- 0.0104 | | SGLang, mono off (stock) | 0.8446 | 0.8302 | An exact per-question McNemar test, mono on against off, finds no difference. For flexible-extract, 87 questions are right only with mono and 79 only without, p = 0.59. For strict-match the counts are 81 and 83, p = 0.94. RULER `niah_single_2` at 128k scores 0.992 with mono on. With MTP, K2 runs only on the verify steps, as the MTP section below describes. GSM8K at concurrency 2 against the same MTP server with the flag off shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8582 against 0.8461, with 85 questions right only with mono and 69 only without, p = 0.23. Strict-match is 0.8446 against 0.8370, p = 0.47. GPQA Diamond and RULER `niah_single_2` ran at concurrency 8, so every decode step is in the mono range. Flag on and flag off use the same server config. | | flag off | flag on | | --- | --- | --- | | GPQA Diamond, thinking, temperature 1.0 (2 runs each) | 0.884, 0.924 (mean 0.904) | 0.894, 0.934 (mean 0.914) | | NIAH 64k (500 questions) | 0.994, 0.996 (2 runs) | 0.996 | | NIAH 128k (500 questions) | 0.996, 1.000 (2 runs) | 0.992 | GPQA samples at temperature 1.0, and the two runs of one arm differ by 4 points, so the 1-point gap is noise. NIAH is greedy. Paired per question, mono against each flag-off run gives p = 0.63 and 0.13 at 128k and p = 1.0 at 64k. The two flag-off runs also disagree with each other on 2 to 5 questions. No difference. The unit tests in `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_5_mono_decode.py` run on 1 GPU. They check that every fp4 byte and e8m0 scale of SGLang's gfx950 expert layout is where K2 reads it. K1 runs at widths 1, 4 and 8 against SGLang's pool layout. It writes the live rows and leaves pad rows and other slots unchanged. With a bf16 state, K1 gives the same core output and conv state as with the widened fp32 state. Its new state equals the new fp32 state rounded to bf16. The tests pass on MI355X in the v0.5.21-based image and on `main`, here the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09 with this branch's files. The file has not run in CI yet. The batch-invariance test in `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_5_mono_batch_invariance.py` runs K1 on 1 GPU and K2 on 8 GPUs. It keeps one probe row fixed and changes the other rows of the step. The probe outputs must be bitwise the same at widths 1 to 8, and equal to the probe run alone. It passes on MI355X on the ROCm 10 `main` nightly. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The numbers in this section are for the head kernels, #60833 `3346929b27`. `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` ran on one 8x MI355X node, TP8, on `main`, here the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09 with this branch's files mounted in both arms. The load is `bench_serving` random, range ratio 0.8, with the same seeds in both arms and one short warm-up cell first. Both servers use the aiter attention backend at page size 16, FSE off and a bf16 SSM state, and only the flag differs. They ran on the same node, back to back. | Cell (prompts) | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Change | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 (8) | 10.88 / 6.86 | -37.0% | 89.3 / 139.2 | +56.0% | | 8k/1k c2 (16) | 12.10 / 8.21 | -32.1% | 158.2 / 230.4 | +45.6% | | 8k/1k c4 (32) | 14.42 / 10.20 | -29.3% | 265.9 / 372.7 | +40.2% | | 8k/1k c8 (64) | 17.08 / 14.37 | -15.9% | 446.8 / 530.4 | +18.7% | | 8k/1k c16 (96), 16 rows: stock path | 23.59 / 23.55 | -0.1% | 650.7 / 655.4 | +0.7% | | 60k/600 c4 (32) | 25.77 / 21.52 | -16.5% | 132.1 / 154.0 | +16.6% | c16 decode steps have more than 8 rows, so they take the stock layers, and that row is the noise floor. TTFT does not change, because prefill is stock. GSM8K on the same servers, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, `lm_eval` local-completions at concurrency 8, shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8491 off against 0.8582 on, paired McNemar p = 0.36. Strict-match is 0.8370 against 0.8476. RULER `niah_single_2` at concurrency 8 scores 0.994 / 0.996 off and 0.992 / 0.998 on, at 64k / 128k. By default on `main`, this checkpoint runs without shared-expert fusion and with an fp32 SSM state, so a default server meets the K2 requirements as it is. These runs set `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` in both arms. ### MTP With speculative decoding on, K1 is off and K2 runs alone on the target-verify steps. GDN layers run SGLang's own input projection and core, then K2 runs `out_proj` and the MoE. K1 cannot run there, because it has no per-draft-token state for the SSM rollback. NEXTN runs 3 draft steps with top-k 1, so a verify step has 4 rows per request, one for each of the 4 draft tokens. Mono covers only c1 with 4 rows and c2 with 8 rows. The K1 requirements on the SSM state dtype and the ReplaySSM ring do not apply then. The MTP A/B uses the same setup plus `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`, so the reference is the same server without the flag. | Cell (prompts) | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Change | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 (8) | 3.87 / 2.88 | -25.7% | 237.8 / 312.1 | +31.2% | | 8k/1k c2 (16) | 4.64 / 3.82 | -17.7% | 391.2 / 463.9 | +18.6% | | 8k/1k c4 (32), 16 rows: stock path | 6.27 / 6.27 | flat | 590.3 / 591.9 | +0.3% | | 60k/600 c1 (8) | 3.95 / 2.97 | -24.9% | 114.4 / 129.3 | +13.0% | The accept length is the same in both arms, 3.62-3.68. GSM8K at concurrency 2 on the same servers shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8597 off against 0.8567 on, paired McNemar p = 0.82. Strict-match is 0.8438 against 0.8446. ### Earlier kernels
The first A/Bs used the #60833 f3c2ec988b kernels. Their tables stay here for reference. The table below compares the first kernels, `f3c2ec988b`, with the next #60833 kernels, `6a1c13b2fc`. Both arms ran on one MI355X node on `main`, the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09 with this branch's files, with a bf16 SSM state and the flag on. | Cell | Median TPOT earlier / new kernels (ms) | Change | Output tok/s earlier / new | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 | 7.77 / 6.88 | -11.5% | 123.4 / 138.0 | +11.8% | | 8k/1k c2 | 9.29 / 8.26 | -11.1% | 203.6 / 227.6 | +11.8% | | 8k/1k c4 | 12.04 / 10.33 | -14.2% | 317.0 / 368.5 | +16.3% | | 8k/1k c8 | 16.56 / 14.50 | -12.4% | 443.0 / 516.9 | +16.7% | | 8k/1k c16, stock path | 23.90 / 23.88 | flat | 643.3 / 645.7 | flat | | 60k/600 c4 | 23.93 / 22.16 | -7.4% | 139.9 / 148.8 | +6.4% | | MTP 8k/1k c1 | 3.26 / 2.90 | -11.0% | 277.8 / 308.3 | +10.9% | | MTP 8k/1k c2 | 4.30 / 3.78 | -12.1% | 418.9 / 469.5 | +12.1% | The whole gain is in K2. In a profile at one row, a K2 launch takes 39.2 us against 50.0 us before. K1 alone measures the same as before. GSM8K paired per question, earlier against new kernels, shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8423 / 0.8537 (p = 0.26) without MTP and 0.8393 / 0.8506 (p = 0.27) with MTP. Strict-match gives p = 0.88 and 0.94. The first A/Bs ran on a v0.5.21-based ROCm image with the same change and the `f3c2ec988b` kernels. That image has identical glue, and the `qwen3_5.py` hunks on its v0.5.21 file. I repeated both A/Bs on `main`, and the results agree. `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, 8x MI355X, TP8, no MTP, `bench_serving` random, range ratio 0.8, the same seeds in both arms. Both servers have FSE off and an fp32 SSM state, and only the flag differs. They ran on the same node, back to back. | Cell (prompts) | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Change | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 (8) | 10.66 / 7.65 | -28.2% | 91.2 / 125.9 | +38.0% | | 8k/1k c2 (16) | 11.68 / 9.12 | -21.9% | 163.8 / 208.3 | +27.2% | | 8k/1k c4 (32), first cell | 14.20 / 11.97 | -15.7% | 265.8 / 265.7 | flat, see below | | 8k/1k c4 (32), warm server | 14.18 / 11.91 | -16.0% | 270.6 / 321.4 | +18.8% | | 8k/1k c8 (64) | 17.51 / 16.39 | -6.4% | 437.6 / 469.1 | +7.2% | | 8k/1k c16 (96), 16 rows: stock path | 23.34 / 23.13 | -0.9% | 656.9 / 664.3 | +1.1% | | 60k/600 c4 (32) | 25.34 / 23.07 | -9.0% | 134.1 / 145.5 | +8.5% | c16 decode steps have more than 8 rows, so they take the stock layers, and that row is the noise floor. TTFT does not change, because prefill is stock. The first c4 cell is flat because of a one-time stall that this PR does not cause. Every server pays 15-40 s on its first prefills, flag on or off. The flag-off server happened to pay it during its startup warm-up request. The stall lines up with first-use JIT compiles on the GDN prefill path. The warm-server row runs one short c4 warm-up cell first. There, Max ITL is 726 ms off and 721 ms on, and the throughput gain matches the TPOT gain. The same A/B on `main` ran on the same node as above, with the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09, this branch's files mounted in both arms and one warm-up cell first. | Cell (prompts) | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Change | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 (8) | 10.99 / 7.76 | -29.4% | 88.5 / 123.6 | +39.7% | | 8k/1k c2 (16) | 12.25 / 9.25 | -24.5% | 156.4 / 205.7 | +31.5% | | 8k/1k c4 (32) | 14.63 / 12.05 | -17.6% | 262.3 / 317.6 | +21.1% | | 8k/1k c8 (64) | 17.30 / 16.48 | -4.7% | 441.2 / 466.6 | +5.7% | | 8k/1k c16 (96), 16 rows: stock path | 23.84 / 23.92 | +0.3% | 643.9 / 644.1 | flat | | 60k/600 c4 (32) | 25.95 / 23.38 | -9.9% | 131.2 / 143.8 | +9.5% | GSM8K on `main` with the same servers shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8582 off against 0.8605 on, with 88 questions right only with mono and 85 only without, p = 0.88. Strict-match is 0.8408 against 0.8415, p = 1.0. #### MTP with the earlier kernels Both arms ran on the same node with FSE off and `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`, so the reference is the same server without the flag. | Cell | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 | 3.77 / 3.21 | 244.5 / 283.3 | +15.9% | | 8k/1k c2 | 4.56 / 4.39 | 400.2 / 413.0 | +3.2% | | 8k/1k c4 (16 rows: stock path) | 6.05 / 6.01 | 608.5 / 606.7 | flat | | 60k/600 c1 | 3.85 / 3.29 | 117.3 / 125.2 | +6.7% | The accept length is the same in both arms, 3.62-3.69. Stock MTP with FSE on gets 3.37 / 4.21 / 5.70 / 3.45 ms TPOT. Its accept length on this random dataset is 3.96-4.00, so its TPOT is not comparable per token. Per verify step, which is TPOT times accept length, K2 saves 14-15% at c1 and 4% at c2 against both. The same A/B on `main` ran on the same node, with the ROCm nightly of 2026-10-09 and this branch's files mounted in both arms. The accept length is 3.62-3.69 in both. | Cell | Median TPOT off / on (ms) | Output tok/s off / on | Change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k c1 | 3.88 / 3.25 | 236.9 / 279.7 | +18.0% | | 8k/1k c2 | 4.62 / 4.29 | 391.0 / 419.0 | +7.1% | | 8k/1k c4 (16 rows: stock path) | 6.31 / 6.28 | 588.0 / 589.3 | flat | | 60k/600 c1 | 3.97 / 3.33 | 114.0 / 123.3 | +8.1% | GSM8K at concurrency 2 on `main` shows no difference. Flexible-extract is 0.8506 off against 0.8499 on, p = 1.0. Strict-match is 0.8385 against 0.8324, p = 0.57.

The merged shape is only faster while the projection is bandwidth bound. 256 + + SGLANG_QWEN3_5_MONO_DECODE + Run Qwen3.8 MXFP4 decode steps of 8 rows or fewer as two persistent FlyDSL launches per layer (gfx950, TP8, needs the shared expert unfused (the default for the Quark MXFP4 checkpoint)). It turns itself off and logs why when a requirement is not met. + false +

@@ -0,0 +1,10 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Kimi-K3 persistent FlyDSL decode kernels for MI355X (gfx950), TP8.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""K2a ``attn_post``: one Kimi-K3 KDA layer from the gated core output to the
+MoE's input row -- o_proj, its TP all-reduce inside the kernel, and the MLP
+AttnRes seam.
+
+One launch a layer and rank, ``BLOCKS`` x ``THREADS``:
+
+    gemv CTAs 56 ..   o_proj (448 x 16 rows, K = 1536 local): bf16 GEMV of the
+                      core rows (plain loads: the previous launch wrote them) ->
+                      bf16 partial -> pushed to every rank's AR region (system
+                      scope, this rank's slot)
+    attn CTAs 0 .. 55 per 128 columns: the 8 ranks' partials summed in rank
+                      order (fp32 -> bf16: the custom all-reduce's result) ->
+                      LDS delta; then K1's AttnRes stages with the MLP's weights:
+                      prefix + delta -> prefix out, the sources' softmax mix,
+                      post_attention_layernorm -> the MoE input x
+
+The AR region is double-buffered by the step epoch's parity: a rank a step
+ahead writes the other half, so no peer's unread partials are overwritten.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import flydsl.compiler as flyc
+import flydsl.expr as fx
+import torch
+from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import buffer_ops as bo
+from flydsl.expr import gpu, range_constexpr
+from flydsl.expr.typing import Int32, Int64, T
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.k3_mono_flydsl.attention.kda import (
+    _SOURCES,
+    COLS,
+    HIDDEN,
+    LDS_PAD,
+    NA,
+    PROJ,
+    ROWS,
+    stage_gate,
+    stage_mix,
+    stage_slice,
+    step_tag,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.k3_mono_flydsl.common.debug import (
+    stamp,
+    stamp_begin,
+    stamp_flush,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.k3_mono_flydsl.common.ops import (
+    CM_NT,
+    bf16_round,
+    ld_i32,
+    mfma_bf16,
+    row_sum,
+    rsrc,
+    traced,
+    uniform,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.k3_mono_flydsl.common.plan import (
+    BLOCKS,
+    THREADS,
+    WAVES,
+    KernelAbi,
+    key_tuple,
+    pair_layout,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.k3_mono_flydsl.common.ranks import peer_bases, sum_partials
+from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.k3_mono_flydsl.common.sync import Mailbox, preg, shift, sreg
+
+TP = 8
+OROWS = HIDDEN  # o_proj rows (full hidden, a rank's K slice)
+OTASKS = OROWS // ROWS  # 448
+OK = PROJ  # K = 1536 a rank
+OKCH = OK // 128  # 12 chunks
+GEMV0 = NA  # the first gemv CTA
+GEMV_N = BLOCKS - NA  # 200
+TL_POINTS = 6  # start, gemv, pushed, reduced, slice/gate, mix
+
+_STREAM = fx.Stream(None)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class AttnPostBuild:
+    tokens: int
+    nblocks: int  # the MLP AttnRes block sources
+    eps: float = 1e-5
+    out_eps: float = 1e-5
+    timeline: bool = False
+
+
+ABI = KernelAbi(
+    (
+        "core",
+        "w_o",
+        "prefix",
+        "blocks",
+        "blk_sm",
+        "blk_sr",
+        "ares_nw",
+        "ares_qk",
+        "in_nw",
+        "x_out",
+        "scratch",
+        "peers",
+        "rank",
+        "epoch",
+        "layer",
+        "tl",
+    )
+)
+
+
+def ar_half_pairs(s):
+    """One parity's AR region: [src rank][token][column pair]."""
+    return TP * s * HIDDEN // 2
+
+
+def peer_bytes(max_tokens):
+    return 2 * ar_half_pairs(max_tokens) * 8
+
+
+def scratch_layout(key: AttnPostBuild) -> dict:
+    s, ns = key.tokens, key.nblocks + 1
+    pairs = {
+        "part": NA * s * ns * 2,
+        "wgt": s * (ns + 1),
+        "msq": NA * s,
+        "xrdy": NA,
+    }
+    return pair_layout(pairs.items())
+
+
+def scratch_bytes(key: AttnPostBuild) -> int:
+    return max(o + n for o, n in scratch_layout(key).values())
+
+
+def o_loads(c, rg):
+    """Rows 16 rg .. of o_proj, this wave's K chunks (wave, wave + 8 < 12): a lane
+    64 B of its row a chunk."""
+    lane, wave = c["lane"], c["wave"]
+    r_w = rsrc(c["args"]["w_o"])
+    row = rg * ROWS + lane % ROWS
+    g = lane // ROWS
+    out = []
+    for i in range(2):
+        ch = fx.min(wave + WAVES * i, OKCH - 1)
+        base = (row * OK + ch * 128 + g * 8) // 2
+        out.append(
+            [
+                fx.Vector(
+                    bo.buffer_load(
+                        r_w,
+                        base + 16 * q,
+                        vec_width=4,
+                        dtype=T.i32,
+                        cache_modifier=CM_NT,
+                    )
+                )
+                for q in range(4)
+            ]
+        )
+    return out
+
+
+@traced
+def load_core(c):
+    """The core rows (S x 1536 bf16) -> LDS, rows padded."""
+    s, tid = c["S"], c["tid"]
+    words = s * OK // 8
+    row = OK + LDS_PAD
+    for i in range_constexpr((words + THREADS - 1) // THREADS):
+        e = fx.min(tid + THREADS * i, words - 1)
+        v = fx.Vector(
+            bo.buffer_load(rsrc(c["args"]["core"]), e * 4, vec_width=4, dtype=T.i32)
+        )
+        t = e // (OK // 8)
+        k = e % (OK // 8) * 8
+        if tid + THREADS * i < words:
+            fx.ptr_store(v, c["xl"] + (t * row + k) // 2)
+    gpu.barrier()
+
+
+@traced
+def stage_o(c, rg, ops):
+    """Rows 16 rg ..: GEMV -> bf16 partials -> every rank's AR region, this
+    rank's slot (thread: token, row pair; a put a peer)."""
+    s, tid, lane, wave, red = c["S"], c["tid"], c["lane"], c["wave"], c["red"]
+    g = lane // ROWS
+    t = fx.min(lane % ROWS, s - 1)
+    row = OK + LDS_PAD
+    acc = fx.Vector.filled(4, 0.0, fx.Float32)
+    for i in range_constexpr(2):
+        ch = wave + WAVES * i
+        live = ch < OKCH
+        k = fx.min(ch, OKCH - 1) * 128 + g * 8
+        for q in range_constexpr(4):
+            xb = fx.Vector(
+                fx.ptr_load(
+                    c["xl"] + (t * row + k + 32 * q) // 2,
+                    result_type=fx.Vector.make_type(4, fx.Int32),
+                )
+            )
+            xb = fx.Vector.from_elements(
+                [live.select(xb[d], fx.Int32(0)) for d in range(4)], fx.Int32
+            )
+            acc = mfma_bf16(
+                ops[i][q].bitcast(fx.BFloat16), xb.bitcast(fx.BFloat16), acc
+            )
+    fx.ptr_store(acc, red + (wave * 64 + lane) * 4)
+    gpu.barrier()
+    if tid < s * (ROWS // 2):
+        tt = tid // (ROWS // 2)
+        rp = tid % (ROWS // 2)
+        v0 = bf16_round(row_sum(red, 2 * rp, tt))
+        v1 = bf16_round(row_sum(red, 2 * rp + 1, tt))
+        at = (c["rank"] * s + tt) * HIDDEN + rg * ROWS + 2 * rp
+        for p in range_constexpr(TP):
+            c["put_bf"](c["ar_peer"][p], at, [v0, v1])
+    gpu.barrier()
+
+
+@traced
+def stage_reduce(c, task):
+    """Columns 128 task ..: the 8 ranks' partials, rank order, -> bf16 delta in
+    LDS (thread: token, column pair)."""
+    s, tid = c["S"], c["tid"]
+    if tid < s * (COLS // 2):
+        t = tid // (COLS // 2)
+        cp = tid % (COLS // 2)
+        col = task * COLS + 2 * cp
+        lo, hi = sum_partials(
+            c["poll"], c["ar_own"], lambda src: ((src * s + t) * HIDDEN + col) // 2, TP
+        )
+        fx.ptr_store(bf16_round(lo), c["delta_lds"] + (t * COLS + 2 * cp))
+        fx.ptr_store(bf16_round(hi), c["delta_lds"] + (t * COLS + 2 * cp + 1))
+    gpu.barrier()
+
+
+_BUILDS: dict = {}
+
+
+def build(key: AttnPostBuild):
+    if key in _BUILDS:
+        return _BUILDS[key]
+    s, ns = key.tokens, key.nblocks + 1
+    assert s * (ROWS // 2) <= THREADS and s * (COLS // 2) <= THREADS
+    lay = scratch_layout(key)
+    half = ar_half_pairs(s) * 8
+
+    @fx.struct
+    class Smem:
+        red: fx.Array[fx.Float32, WAVES * 64 * 4, 16]
+        xl: fx.Array[fx.Int32, s * (OK + LDS_PAD) // 2, 16]
+        vals: fx.Array[fx.Float32, s * ns * COLS, 16]
+        dl: fx.Array[fx.Float32, s * COLS, 16]
+        tls: fx.Array[fx.Int64, TL_POINTS, 16]
+
+    keyed = key_tuple(key, _SOURCES)
+    name = f"k3_mono_attn_post_s{s}_nb{key.nblocks}_t{int(key.timeline)}"
+
+    @flyc.kernel(name=name, known_block_size=[THREADS, 1, 1])
+    def attn_post(
+        core: Int64,
+        w_o: Int64,
+        prefix: Int64,
+        blocks: Int64,
+        blk_sm: Int32,
+        blk_sr: Int32,
+        ares_nw: Int64,
+        ares_qk: Int64,
+        in_nw: Int64,
+        x_out: Int64,
+        scratch: Int64,
+        peers: Int64,
+        rank: Int32,
+        epoch: Int64,
+        layer: Int32,
+        tl: Int64,
+    ):
+        _ = keyed
+        tid = fx.thread_idx.x
+        bid = fx.block_idx.x
+        lds = fx.SharedAllocator().allocate(Smem).peek()
+        mb = Mailbox(step_tag(epoch, layer) - 1)
+        par = uniform(ld_i32(epoch, 0)) % 2
+        bases = peer_bases(peers, TP)
+        c = {
+            "S": s,
+            "NS": ns,
+            "NB": key.nblocks,
+            "tid": tid,
+            "bid": bid,
+            "lane": tid % 64,
+            "wave": tid // 64,
+            "rank": rank,
+            "delta": True,
+            "debug": False,
+            "eps": key.eps,
+            "out_eps": key.out_eps,
+            "put": mb.put,
+            "put_bf": mb.put_bf,
+            "poll": mb.poll,
+            "red": lds.red.ptr,
+            "xl": lds.xl.ptr,
+            "vals": lds.vals.ptr,
+            "delta_lds": lds.dl.ptr,
+            "xbuf": x_out,
+            "ar_peer": [shift(preg(b, 0, "ar"), fx.Int64(par) * half) for b in bases],
+            "ar_own": shift(preg(load_own(peers, rank), 0, "ar"), fx.Int64(par) * half),
+            "args": {
+                "core": core,
+                "w_o": w_o,
+                "prefix": prefix,
+                "blocks": blocks,
+                "blk_sm": blk_sm,
+                "blk_sr": blk_sr,
+                "ares_nw": ares_nw,
+                "ares_qk": ares_qk,
+                "in_nw": in_nw,
+                "x_dbg": 0,
+            },
+        }
+        for region in ("part", "wgt", "msq", "xrdy"):
+            c[region] = sreg(scratch, lay[region][0], region)
+        on, tls = key.timeline, lds.tls.ptr
+        stamp_begin(on, tls, tid, TL_POINTS)
+        if bid >= GEMV0:
+            gi = bid - GEMV0
+            # every task's weights in flight first: nothing here polls
+            ops = [o_loads(c, fx.min(gi + GEMV_N * j, OTASKS - 1)) for j in range(3)]
+            load_core(c)
+            stamp(on, tls, tid, 1)
+            for j in range_constexpr(3):
+                if gi + GEMV_N * j < OTASKS:
+                    stage_o(c, gi + GEMV_N * j, ops[j])
+            stamp(on, tls, tid, 2)
+        if bid < NA:
+            stage_reduce(c, bid)
+            stamp(on, tls, tid, 3)
+            stage_slice(c, bid)
+            if bid < s:
+                stage_gate(c, bid)
+            stamp(on, tls, tid, 4)
+            stage_mix(c, bid)
+            stamp(on, tls, tid, 5)
+        stamp_flush(on, tls, tl, tid, bid, TL_POINTS)
+
+    @flyc.jit
+    def launch(
+        core: Int64,
+        w_o: Int64,
+        prefix: Int64,
+        blocks: Int64,
+        blk_sm: Int32,
+        blk_sr: Int32,
+        ares_nw: Int64,
+        ares_qk: Int64,
+        in_nw: Int64,
+        x_out: Int64,
+        scratch: Int64,
+        peers: Int64,
+        rank: Int32,
+        epoch: Int64,
+        layer: Int32,
+        tl: Int64,
+        stream: fx.Stream = _STREAM,
+    ):
+        _ = keyed
+        attn_post(
+            core,
+            w_o,
+            prefix,
+            blocks,
+            blk_sm,
+            blk_sr,
+            ares_nw,
+            ares_qk,
+            in_nw,
+            x_out,
+            scratch,
+            peers,
+            rank,
+            epoch,
+            layer,
+            tl,
+        ).launch(grid=(BLOCKS,), block=(THREADS,), stream=stream)
+
+    ABI.check(attn_post, launch)
+    _BUILDS[key] = launch
+    return launch
+
+
+def load_own(peers, rank):
+    """This rank's own peer buffer base (its entry of the table)."""
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.moe.k3_mono_flydsl.common.ops import load_ptr64
+
+    return load_ptr64(peers, rank)
+
+
+def attn_post(
+    key: AttnPostBuild,
+    *,
+    core,
+    w_o,
+    prefix,
+    blocks,
+    ares_nw,
+    ares_qk,
+    in_nw,
+    x_out,
+    scratch,
+    peers,
+    rank,
+    epoch,
+    layer,
+    tl=None,
+):
+    """Host launcher. ``peers``: the int64 table of every rank's peer buffer
+    (at least ``peer_bytes(S)`` each); ``prefix`` updated in place."""
+    assert w_o.shape == (OROWS, OK) and w_o.is_contiguous()
+    assert prefix.is_contiguous() and core.is_contiguous() and x_out.is_contiguous()
+    f = build(key)
+    f(
+        core.data_ptr(),
+        w_o.data_ptr(),
+        prefix.data_ptr(),
+        blocks.data_ptr(),
+        blocks.stride(0),
+        blocks.stride(1),
+        ares_nw.data_ptr(),
+        ares_qk.data_ptr(),
+        in_nw.data_ptr(),
+        x_out.data_ptr(),
+        scratch.data_ptr(),
+        peers.data_ptr(),
+        rank,
+        epoch.data_ptr(),
+        layer,
+        0 if tl is None else tl.data_ptr(),
+        stream=torch.cuda.current_stream(),
+    )
